title: Console onboarding tour: first-run checklist visual heuristics pack
creator: Asha Malik
description: Deliver a cohesive visual asset pack and screenshot set for the Console first-run onboarding tour. Includes: high-fidelity checklist cards, empty-state illustrations (light/dark), micro-animation specs for progress states, localized screenshot variants (EN/FR/DE), tips tooltip treatments, and a distribution-ready slices folder for release notes and marketing. Assets must support Dedicated and Private deployment flows where the checklist branches differ (e.g., 'Connect Dedicated Pool' vs 'Enable VPC Peering'). The pack should prioritize low visual noise and accessible contrast while demonstrating progressive disclosure of advanced settings.
acceptance_criteria: Checklist cards exported as 2 density variants (compact, roomy) PNG and SVG
Empty-state illustrations exported for light and dark themes with 4:3 and 16:9 crops
Tooltip tips have copy reviewed by PM and localized for EN/FR/DE
Micro-animation Lottie exports under 120KB and documented with trigger rules
All screenshots match latest Console UI and are validated by QA on staging
comments: 2026-03-09 Asha: Initial brief posted. Emphasis on accessible color contrasts and small file sizes for embedded emails.

2026-03-12 Eng-review: Requested separate screenshots for user role Admin vs Developer to show RBAC hints.
2026-03-13 Accessibility review: Contrast for tip text increased to 4.8:1. Also added focus-visible states for keyboard navigation.

decision_log: Use progressive disclosure for advanced settings: show collapsed 'Advanced' row within checklist cards rather than separate screens.
Prefer single illustration set with color tints for Dedicated/Private variants to reduce production effort.
Micro-animations will be Lottie JSON with a fallback static SVG for environments that block animated assets.
Localization: only translate tooltip text and checklist step labels for initial release (EN/FR/DE); screenshots will be localized in follow-up patch if needed.
